inputs.text: This looks like a coordinated attempt to repackage abortion access as a religious-liberty issue so the courts can weaken a prolife law while presenting it as neutral protection of rights. The ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice made the claim, and Judge Christina R. [...] blocked the law. The post’s title, “This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right,” frames the dispute bluntly—but the bigger concern is how institutions can use noble-sounding principles to advance an agenda while avoiding the real question at stake.
